title: Fitness app backend on a small Kubernetes cluster

organisation.name: Pocketfit
organisation.summary: Pocketfit makes a workout and step-tracking app with 400,000 users. The mobile app calls an API gateway that checks OAuth tokens issued by the auth service and routes requests to API pods on a small managed Kubernetes cluster. Profiles, health metrics and location history live in a NoSQL table; progress photos go straight from the phone to a storage bucket through signed upload URLs. A push notification service reminds users to train. One build pipeline builds the app and the backend images and deploys to the cluster with a stored cluster credential.

api_security.summary: The profile endpoint returns any user's profile when the id in the path changes
Access tokens never expire, so a token copied from a phone works for months

application_security.summary: Photo download URLs last a week and are built from sequential ids
The "import photo from a link" feature fetches any address, including the metadata service

container_kubernetes.summary: The pipeline's stored cluster-admin credential can run anything in the cluster
The cluster API endpoint is reachable from the internet

cloud_security.summary: The API pods' cloud role reads and writes the whole user table and the photos bucket
A bucket policy change lets anyone list the photos bucket

identity_access.summary: Access tokens never expire and are not bound to a device
Passwords reused from other breaches sign in to member accounts

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: The CI secrets hold the app signing key, the push key and the cluster credential together
A malicious package runs during the backend build

data_security.summary: Health and location history can be pulled out through the API by any signed-in user
Progress photos are reachable through week-long download links

zero_trust.summary: The API pods trust a user id header that only the gateway is supposed to set
Inside the cluster every pod can reach the API server and every other pod

network_security.summary: The cluster API server listens on a public address
The API pods' load balancer is reachable directly, skipping the gateway

reviewNotes: Beginner: object-level authorisation missing in the API, non-expiring tokens, a public cluster endpoint and a cluster-admin CI credential.
